subjects.displayTitle: The mission of the Manifestation: educating hearts and renewing the world
subjects.introduction: Asked why He had come into the world, Bahá’u’lláh is reported to have answered with a picture: a day when a young woman adorned with jewels could travel alone from the east to the west and return home untouched, because trustworthiness and justice had become general. The mission of the Manifestation of God is measured by that ordinary safety, and by what must change in people for it to exist. He has come, He says, to draw out the essence hidden in every stone, to quench hatred, to forbid bloodshed, to array every soul in a saintly character. The Prophets train human beings out of the thralldom of instinct and bring to light capacities that were always there, bearing calumny and prison to do it. Jesus announced His own mission in Nazareth as good news to the poor, sight to the blind and release to the captives [1]. The journey leads on to the Manifestation as physician, as educator and as sun, and to what religion is for in a single life and in a whole society.
subjects.arc: Begin with a concrete vision of safety and trust, explore character and human unity, then follow guidance, education, sacrifice, and the awakening of capacities into shared responsibility.

order.why: Consider organic unity and love for the whole human race.
Open with the reported vision of safe travel and the extraction of hidden human potential.
shortened: Let Me tell you that you may know: I have come so that in this world full of corruption, where the door of tranquility has been utterly shut to all beings through the oppression of the oppressors and the treachery of the treacherous, I may, by God's might and power, establish such justice, protection, trustworthiness and religion throughout all regions--manifest and resplendent--that if one of those maidens secluded behind veils, whose radiant beauty would count the sun itself as but a mote, and who in all aspects of grace and beauty would have no peer or likeness, were to emerge from behind the veil adorned with the most precious jewels and ornaments beyond the reckoning of the wise, and travel alone, unaccompanied and unhindered, from the East of creation to the West of invention, wandering through every land and journeying through every clime, such would be the trustworthiness, religiousness, justice, and fairness, and such the absence of treachery, baseness, tyranny and inequity, that no hand of aggression or greed would stretch forth toward the hem of her wealth, nor would any lustful or iniquitous eye turn to gaze upon her sanctified beauty, until she returns to her dwelling and homeland with an unsullied heart and a radiant countenance." Then He said: "By God's power, I shall transform the world in this way and shall open this most great door unto the face of all peoples."

The Fifth Treasure: When the Ancient Beauty opened the gate of joy and glad-tidings to the face of the people of creation, He spoke this supreme word: "I have come to this world to extract essences. If there exists an atom of essence in a stone behind the seven seas, I will not cease until I have extracted that essence from it."

order.why: Make the concrete virtues of trustworthiness, kindness, and uprightness central.
shortened: The purpose of the one true God in manifesting Himself is to summon all mankind to truthfulness and sincerity, to piety and trustworthiness, to resignation and submissiveness to the Will of God, to forbearance and kindliness, to uprightness and wisdom. His object is to array every man with the mantle of a saintly character, and to adorn him with the ornament of holy and goodly deeds.

order.why: Read the stated aim of quenching hatred and animosity.
shortened: He hath had no purpose except to quench the fire of hatred and animosity which blazeth in the hearts of the peoples.

order.why: Connect the rejection of bloodshed and strife with cleansing hearts.
Read edification, progress, fellowship, and human glory as linked purposes.
shortened: We say that the purpose underlying the advent of the Kingdom is the edification of the souls of men, the progress of the world of humanity, the manifestation of the love of God, the establishment of fellowship and unity amongst all peoples, the appearance of divine perfections, and the realization of the glory of the human race. This is the purpose of the advent of the Kingdom, and this is its result.

order.why: Hear the reported invitation to become heralds of happiness.
Consider truth, sincerity, love, and faithfulness as fruits for living in this world.
Read education of people and improvement of lands together.
Connect reformation of the world with the human station.
shortened: He hath appeared for the reformation of the world, and counseleth all with that which will manifest man's station in creation.

order.why: Hear the testimony to advancement of existence.
shortened: The world and its peoples bear witness that this Wronged One hath desired naught save the exaltation of the Word and the advancement of existence.

order.why: Read mercy and tranquility as intended gifts.
shortened: He has come with the truth to adorn the world with mercy and tranquility, but most of the people do not understand.

order.why: Consider the elixir image through comfort and human exaltation.
Retain the brief statement joining world reform and the life of nations.
shortened: He hath come for the reformation of the world and the life of nations.

order.why: Read the paired aims of reforming the world and refining nations.
shortened: O concourse of men! He Who was promised in the Books of God hath come, He Whose remembrance was treasured in the hearts of the Messengers. He hath come to reform the world and refine the nations.

order.why: Consider the source’s contrast between a reforming purpose and lack of awareness.
shortened: He hath come for the reformation of the world, but the people are unaware.

order.why: Keep the personal address to Jabbar and its interpretation of the name.
shortened: O Jabbar! The meaning of this name is manifest and evident today, for the Countenance of the Desired One hath appeared for the reformation of the world, yet most are veiled and deprived thereof.

order.why: Read the theme of world reform alongside the source’s account of rejection.
Hear the concise first-person statement of mission.
Keep the lifelong account of opposition beside the purpose of edification.
shortened: Say: Throughout His entire life this Wronged One hath been in the hands of His enemies, and hath had and hath no purpose except the reformation of the world and the edification of its peoples.

order.why: Read the lament over tyranny in relation to life and reform.
shortened: He hath come for the life of the world and the reformation of the nations, yet they have risen against Him with such tyranny as hath caused the Concourse on High to lament and those who circle round the Throne at eventide and at dawn to weep.

order.why: Explore the common tree and rose-garden as images of solidarity.
shortened: The Blessed Perfection hath appeared for the sole purpose of the unification and solidarity of the people of the world, so that all of them may enter under the shade of one tree, sing one melody in one rose-garden and adorn the universe with love and oneness.

order.why: Read the call for present effort to unite humanity.
Keep the public address’s account of changed relationships in the East attributed.
shortened: In the Orient there were great differences among races and peoples. They hated each other, and there was no association among them. Various and divergent sects were hostile, irreconcilable. The different races were in constant war and conflict. About sixty years ago Baha'u'llah appeared upon the eastern horizon. He caused love and unity to become manifest among these antagonistic peoples. He united them with the bond of love; their former hatred and animosity passed away; love and unity reigned instead.

order.why: Read the reported shared aim of prophets, sages, and philosophers.
shortened: Consider how the Prophets Who have been sent, the great souls who have appeared and the sages who have arisen in the world have exhorted mankind to unity and love. This has been the essence of their mission and teaching. This has been the goal of their guidance and message. The Prophets, saints, seers and philosophers have sacrificed their lives in order to establish these principles and teachings amongst men.

order.why: Consider the reported messengers as specialists in love and healing between nations.
Hear the reported mission of binding, healing, and illuminating.
Read the reported definition of heavenly wisdom as peace and reconciliation.
shortened: For this all the Divine Messengers became manifest-to teach the Heavenly Wisdom. This Heavenly Wisdom is eternal peace, universal reconciliation, and unending rest for man.

order.why: Keep the reported criteria of universal civilization, peace, and virtue together.
shortened: Ninthly: He must be the Establisher of Universal Civilization; the Unifier of religions, the standard-bearer of universal Peace and the embodiment of all the highest and noblest virtues of the world of humanity.

order.why: Consider the reported shepherd gathering scattered flocks.
Read the reported physician who strengthens and renews a world.
Explore the reported gardener’s transformation of fruitless and withered trees.
shortened: Through the Divine Gardener, under the shadow of God's mercy, certain souls are trained and educated. He changes unfruitful trees into fruitful ones; dried trees into fresh trees; and under his direction every kind of useful tree is planted, while many and fragrant flowers grow.

order.why: Read the reported seed that develops into many forms of advancement.
Consider the public address’s mirror reflecting light and love.
shortened: The mission of the Prophets, the revelation of the Holy Books, the manifestation of the heavenly Teachers and the purpose of divine philosophy all center in the training of the human realities so that they may become clear and pure as mirrors and reflect the light and love of the Sun of Reality.

order.why: Read the planting of knowledge in good soil by the hands of will.
shortened: Every aware soul beareth witness that this Wronged One hath summoned the people to the most exalted horizon and commanded them to that which profiteth them. The purpose is that all hearts might be illumined with the lights of true divine unity and that the saplings of the knowledge of God - exalted be His glory - might be planted by the hands of will in pure and goodly soil.

order.why: Explore spiritual virtues as suns rising from human beings.
shortened: All the Prophets and Messengers were sent by the Lord of the worlds so that, through the endeavors of those holy souls, the suns of spiritual virtues might shine forth from the horizons of human temples.

order.why: Read the sending of educators to adorn people with divine attributes.
Consider education, conscience, and spiritual perfections together.
Hear the succinct statement of education and manifested perfection.
shortened: The purpose of the appearance of the Promised Beauty was that human souls be educated and become manifestations of divine perfections.

order.why: Defines the prophetic mission as the education and guidance of humanity.
Read the public address’s account of awakening latent capacities.
Consider training that frees people from domination by instinct.
shortened: God has purposed that the darkness of the world of nature shall be dispelled and the imperfect attributes of the natal self be effaced in the effulgent reflection of the Sun of Truth. The mission of the Prophets of God has been to train the souls of humanity and free them from the thralldom of natural instincts and physical tendencies.

order.why: Read the reported distinction of virtues from vices through education.
Keep the reported lists of vices and virtues as an account of transformation.
Consider the reported readjustment of ethical relationships.
shortened: The Holy Divine Manifestations have appeared in this world to instruct mankind in the school of morality and to readjust their ethical relations. For without faith and sanctification the moral fiber of the children of men will not be improved.

order.why: Read the reported education of spirit and manifestation of grace.
Hear the reported purpose of bringing latent perfections into view.
Consider the reported movement from undeveloped capacity toward recognition.
Read the public address’s universal-educator claim in its own historical language.
shortened: The Prophets of God are the first Educators. They bestow universal education upon man and cause him to rise from the lowest levels of savagery to the highest pinnacles of spiritual development.

order.why: Hear the reported link between education, life, and salvation.
Consider the reported emphasis on training as the outcome of mission.
Retain the reported acquired virtues and its existing omission.
shortened: All the philosophers have come with the intention of teaching man to acquire virtues. All the prophets who have come have come to endow man with acquired virtues...

order.why: Read inner perception and the human temple adorned with grace.
shortened: They come to educate and illuminate mankind, to bestow spiritual susceptibilities, to quicken inner perceptions and thereby adorn the reality of man -- the human temple -- with divine graces. Through Them man may become the point of the emanations of God and the recipient of heavenly bounties.

order.why: Keep the reported account of Christ’s educational purpose.
Read the reported appeal to Christendom through Christ’s example and renewed guidance.
shortened: O Christendom! Did not Christ have to live a pure, perfect earthly life as an eternally shining example to his deluded contemporaries; did not He, the great Master, have to refresh and teach again the Revelation, the guidance of God, and imbue with the laws and ordinances of the All-Highest a generation gone astray, blind and deaf?

order.why: Read the reported bestowal of spiritual life through heavenly bounty.
shortened: All the prophets of God have come for the purpose of bestowing upon men the heavenly bounties, in order that through the breaths of the Holy Spirit man might be resuscitated and thus become the noblest of creatures.

order.why: Consider the reported contrasts of darkness and light, death and life.
Read the reported heavenly table as virtues nourishing spiritual life.
Consider the reported care of spiritual as well as bodily development.
Keep the reported reference to institutions within the broad scope of mission.
shortened: These holy Manifestations of God establish eternal institutions for humanity in all worlds, even in this dusty realm, but alas that human souls do not appreciate their worth.

order.why: Read the reported need for divine instruction and inspiration.
Consider the reported relation between a teacher’s contemporaries and wider historical conditions.
shortened: On the one hand, each of these great teachers had to meet a problem peculiar to himself-that of guiding and satisfying his contemporaries and associates; and, on the other, the condition of the world's advancement in general-the state of communication between different parts of the world-was such that the teachings of each were confined to the people of that region to which they came and for whom they were especially adapted.

order.why: Read the sending of Messengers and Books to disclose a path.
Consider hearing purified of misleading tales and attuned to divine utterance.
Read guidance through commandments and Books, retaining the particular place assigned to the Furqan.
shortened: He it is Who sent forth the Messengers to exalt His Word, to manifest His commandments, to establish His laws, and revealed unto them the Books for the guidance of His servants and creation, until it culminated in the Book that distinguished between truth and falsehood, which was named the Furqan in the kingdom of utterance, and was made an enduring testimony for all who dwell in the realm of possibility.

order.why: Keep righteousness, warning, and glad tidings together in the City of Unity.
shortened: Know ye that the Exalted One hath in truth sent forth the Messengers to bid men to righteousness and piety, to forbid them from transgression and wickedness, and to give them glad tidings of the meeting with God on the Day when light shall shine forth from a seat of transcendent glory.

order.why: Consider guidance as preventing tyranny and corruption.
Hear the account of Messengers as bearers of warning and glad tidings.
shortened: He hath sent forth the Messengers as bearers of glad-tidings and warners, that they might give the people tidings of a holy and resplendent Paradise."

order.why: Read the Messenger’s duty of conveying the message.
Consider the speaker’s purpose of delivering what was entrusted.
Read the relation between inaccessible divine knowledge and the sending of guides.
shortened: And since the gate of attainment was closed and people were debarred from knowledge of the hidden treasure, He chose pure essences and holy souls and sent them from the higher realm to the kingdom of creation, that they might guide all and lead them to the straight path.

order.why: Consider Messengers as lamps and turning toward them as turning toward God.
Keep the Bab’s testimony to Muhammad’s stations of knowledge and love.
Read the benediction on the guide to the straight path and those who followed.
Keep the account of the prophetic chain and Muhammad within its source’s theological voice.
Read the account of the Bab’s preparatory mission and martyrdom.
shortened: The Primal Point, namely the Herald of the Most Great Beauty, gave the people glad tidings that they might purify and prepare their hearts. Before His mission was complete, the divines of Persia pronounced the sentence of His death and martyred Him. Thereafter the Most Great Luminary rent asunder the veil, and through His Revelation the worlds of Command and Creation were perfected and established.

order.why: Consider the reported renewal of an earlier foundation.
Read the account of universal Manifestations inaugurating renewed life.
shortened: Through Their advent the world of existence is renewed, a new cycle is inaugurated, a new religion is revealed, souls are quickened to a new life, and East and West are flooded with light. These Souls are the universal Manifestations of God and have been sent forth to the entire world and the generality of mankind.

order.why: Hear the reported image of light shed through teaching.
shortened: It was to manifest this light that Baha'u'llah was born, and came into the world. He taught Eternal Truth to men, and shed the rays of Divine Light in all lands.

order.why: Consider the reported purpose of enabling a person to guide others in turn.
shortened: God sent His Prophets into the world to teach and enlighten man, to explain to him the mystery of the Power of the Holy Spirit, to enable him to reflect the light, and so in his turn, to be the source of guidance to others.

order.why: Read the public address’s account of disciples learning from conduct and carrying teaching outward.
shortened: When Christ appeared, certain blessed souls followed His example. They were with their Master, ever watching and observing His conduct, movements and thoughts. They witnessed the persecutions which were heaped upon Him and were informed of all the events appertaining to that marvelous life -- recipients of His kindness and favors. After the ascension of Christ they hastened to various regions of the world, scattering broadcast the teachings and instructions which He had given them.

order.why: Keep the reported instruction to Mulla Husayn concerning teaching and quickening souls.
shortened: Ere we depart, we shall appoint unto each of the eighteen souls his special mission, and shall send them forth to accomplish their task. We shall instruct them to teach the Word of God and to quicken the souls of men.

order.why: Make the reported role of human will explicit in following the path shown.
shortened: The fields and flowers of the Spiritual Realm are pointed out to us by the Manifestations who walk amid their glories. It remains for the soul of man to follow them in these paths of eternal life, through the exercise of its own human will.

order.why: Read the reported development of will-power for unity and practical prosperity.
Consider the reported distinction between receiving praise and educating people.
Read the reported independence from fame and the focus on educating souls.
shortened: These are idle fancies because those holy Beings knew well that the dominion of God existed when there was no trace of them and that it shall continue to exist when no trace of them remains. Thus fame or oblivion, honor or degradation are one and the same to those Gems of existence. Indeed, their ultimate desire is selfless devotion to the one true God and absolute nothingness in His court. Their only motive has been the education of blessed souls and sanctified beings who are the foundation of divine education and promoters of the most great guidance and the supreme favor.

order.why: Keep the reported interpretation of Christ’s mission in its particular conversation.
Hear the assertion of seeking others’ nearness rather than advantage for oneself.
Read the stated intention to benefit people in this world and the next.
Consider divine love and bounty as the reason for sending Messengers.
Hear the testimony to nearness and benefit beyond this world.
Read the command toward what profits humanity.
shortened: Say: He, verily, is the One Who speaketh the truth and commandeth the people to that which profiteth them in this world and the next, yet most of the people know not.

order.why: Retain the brief aim of guiding and drawing people near.
Connect purification from vain desire with nearness.
shortened: The Glory (Baha) hath come unto you to purify you from vain desire and draw you nigh unto God, the Lord of the first and the last.

order.why: Keep the reported preparation for death within the purpose of education.
shortened: The prophets and the messengers have come in order to guide mankind to the straight path of the True One. Their aim has been no other than the education of the people, so that at the time of death they may depart to the Supreme Friend, with perfect sanctification, purification, and severance.

order.why: Consider the reported relationship between shared suffering and the ability to guide.
Read the reported connection between sacrifice and raising a people.
shortened: And besides security and inherent purpose, one who has no intention to educate and advance humankind and does not sacrifice their life in God's path - how can such a one raise a nation from the depths of abasement to the heights of glory and happiness?

order.why: Keep persecution and calumny within the reported cost of education.
shortened: In this station they occupy themselves with the education of mankind. They have, as a result, to bear the enmity, persecution and calumny of the people.

order.why: Read the reported endurance of hardship for human attainment.
Consider the reported trials undertaken for freedom from captivity to nature.
Read the extended transformation of wilderness, darkness, and ignorance through divine education.
Hear the brief statement of tribulation accepted for the world’s salvation.
shortened: We have accepted tribulations for the salvation of the world, yet the peoples remain wrapped in a thick veil.

order.why: Read guidance continuing in imprisonment.
Keep Abdu’l-Baha’s own account of imprisonment and unity distinct from the Manifestations’ mission.
shortened: I am a herald of the Kingdom and a banner of peace and tranquility.

Souls were educated under the shadow of the Word of God who, by hundreds and thousands, strove to spread eternal life, turned toward the Kingdom of God, sacrificed their lives in the field of martyrdom, and finally I chose this prison for myself, meaning I was content to be imprisoned and become the cause of spreading divine love and the unity and oneness of the human world.

order.why: Retain the reported account of ceaseless teaching in its own wording.
Read the reported spiritual vocabulary of giving life, sight, and nourishment.
shortened: I give sight to the blind, hearing to the deaf, the power of speech to the mute and knowledge to the ignorant. I raise the dead, I deliver those who are in darkness and guide them into the realm of Light. I make the poor rich and the weak powerful. I satisfy the hungry ones with the Bread of life and allay the thirst of the thirsty ones with the pure Water of Immortality. This is my work.

order.why: Consider the disturbance and joy accompanying the summons.
Read the temple that speaks truth and summons humanity to illumination.
Hear the prayerful account of being raised to summon creation to life.
Consider the commission to kindle love and draw people toward mercy.
shortened: Thou art He, O my God, Who hath raised me up at Thy behest, and bidden me to occupy Thy seat, and to summon all men to the court of Thy mercy. It is Thou Who hast commanded me to tell out the things Thou didst destine for them in the Tablet of Thy decree and didst inscribe with the pen of Thy Revelation, and Who hast enjoined on me the duty of kindling the fire of Thy love in the hearts of Thy servants, and of drawing all the peoples of the earth nearer to the habitation of Thy throne.

order.why: Read life-giving revelation as unlocking treasures.
shortened: We came to give life to the world and revealed that which unlocks the treasures, yet the people remain in doubt and dissension.

order.why: Hear the concise declaration of coming for the life of the world.
Close with the seal’s brief affirmation of the Beloved who gives life to worlds.

questions: What does the opening vision of safe travel reveal about the relationship between personal virtue and social conditions?
How do educator, physician, gardener, and sun each illuminate a different aspect of the Manifestation’s mission?
What capacities do these readings suggest already exist within human beings, and what helps bring them into action?
How does Jesus’ declaration in Luke 4:16–21 deepen the inquiry into healing, release, and renewal?
What do the passages on suffering and freedom from fame suggest about the purpose and cost of spiritual education?
How might a community assess whether its response to a Messenger is bringing greater trust, unity, and happiness?

references.label: 1 · Luke 4:16–21 · Good news, healing, and release
references.note: Read the King James Version’s account of Jesus reading Isaiah in Nazareth and declaring its fulfillment. Attend to the poor, the brokenhearted, captives, and those needing sight or release. Compare this announced mission with the compilation’s accounts of education, healing, and social renewal while retaining the Gospel’s particular claim about Jesus.

subjects.displayTitle: Humor: affection, perspective, and the art of laughter
subjects.introduction: Bahá’u’lláh is remembered asking that two of every twenty-four hours be spent in a way that brings happiness, and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá called joking the salt of conversation: without it, He said, we would get depressed. It is a startling place to find laughter, among exiles and prisoners, yet that is exactly where it lived. A general who hanged whom he pleased is disarmed by a pun about corrupters of religion; a weary pen is threatened with the whip until it gallops to the end of the page; new dentures become a mutinous foreign garrison. Beneath the play run affection, consolation for the dismissed and the grieving, and a sharp eye for pretension, whether the theologian who cannot swim or the guest who praises contentment after eating his host’s only goat. Ecclesiastes sets a time to laugh beside a time to weep [1], and timing matters, since a joke can carry old stereotypes and real violence as easily as kindness. The trail leads on into happiness and its kinship with sorrow, and into the recollections of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s own life.
subjects.arc: Begin with encouragement and joy, explore affectionate correspondence and the correction of pretension, then examine the tensions of satire before returning to companionship and a wider horizon.

order.why: Read the reported place of happiness amid the risk of discouragement.
shortened: Abdul Baha: Sometimes joking is necessary. Otherwise we would get depressed. The Blessed Beauty said, 'In every twenty-four hours, two hours must be spent in a way that will cause happiness.'

order.why: Open with the reported wireless reply to spiritual discouragement.
Read the Tablet’s joy and jest within imprisonment.
shortened: The Word of God, even if limited to a single word, cannot be equaled by all the books of the world. Grieve not that We have made this Tablet brief, for within it can be seen a mighty Book. This is a Tablet that hath been mixed with the salt of God. When thou hast tasted it and discovered its savor, arise and say: Praise be unto Thee, O God of the worlds! Marvel not if We jest in prison, for sorrows have never overtaken Us in the path of thy Lord, and We are in wondrous joy.

order.why: Consider the reported salt-of-conversation image.
Keep the qualified account of prophetic jest in its own wording.
Consider the reported peacock image and the direction of attention.
Bring laughter into the practical responsibility of giving to the poor.
shortened: He laughed and, still laughing, said: "Assuredly, give to the poor. If you give them only words, when they put their hands into their pockets after you have gone, they will find themselves none the richer for you!"

order.why: Read humor used to answer a threatening political accusation.
Compare the separate reported account of the encounter with Jamal Pasha.
Place stories and jokes within the reported nightly family gathering.
Notice shared laughter in the telling and translation of an image.
shortened: There is some wood that is very dry; it catches fire quickly and burns well. There is other wood that is so wet that it will not burn even though you should try for a whole day. There is no result but smoke. It will not blaze, it will not keep anyone warm; it will not even cook anything! As he said the latter he smiled.
But when Ruha Khanum translated it, Cora laughed out loud. That seemed to delight the Master, for he laughed very heartily with the most unaffected enjoyment.

order.why: Read the explicit desire to bring joy through correspondence.
Consider consolation during dismissal and distress.
shortened: Although for some time you have become my partner and companion, and fallen victim to the aggression of every oppressor, do not grieve and seek not sorrow. I hope that this lowest point of obscurity will be transformed to the heights of acceptance, and the means of joy and gladness will be made ready.

Although the spiritual friends experience continuous and sustained divine joy, if spiritual and physical happiness are joined together it becomes joy upon joy and light upon light. Surely it will become better and more pleasant and more attractive and more satisfying and sweeter. I jest so that you may laugh and be pleased.

order.why: Hear companionship in another person’s sadness beneath the jest.
shortened: Do not grieve, do not be troubled. I am your companion and, God willing, kind to you.

If you show any laxity it will be upon my neck, and if you commit any shortcoming I will be accused, for we are united in condition and partnership in all circumstances. For in these days affairs are confused - a companion is held accountable for his companion's offense.
In any case, this was in jest. The point is that I am saddened by your sadness.

order.why: Read the stated use of jest to change the mood amid tribulation.
Keep the recognition of hardship alongside its explicitly playful language.
shortened: Indeed during this journey you have endured many hardships. No matter, it will pass. As the poet says, "This time will pass, and afterward you will know the value of wellbeing," for companionship with the nightingale and peacock has a different sweetness after being afflicted with the company of the ill-omened crow. Soon you will find deliverance, but if God assists, you have no choice but to flee. Anyway, these were jokes.

order.why: Consider affectionate companionship expressed through the gambling metaphor.
shortened: O Hakim! It is pleasant to joke with you and brings joy. From the ruins of a house of unbaked clay that remained, you gave that away too. Now neither nest nor dwelling remains. You have become a pure gambler. Now rest. They say pure gambling is life-gambling and the ultimate in gambling. Praise be to God that in this field you are the confidant and intimate of 'Abdu'l-Baha. When two paupers sing the same tune, it makes God laugh.

order.why: Read the mock complaint about a friend’s unshared celebrations.
Keep the greeting of a new child and its stated wish to bring joy.
shortened: O you who are firm in the Covenant!

According to the indications and glad tidings of the honored ladies, God has bestowed upon you a noble son who is of utmost beauty and grace, that is, he is second to your other one of sacred titles. Therefore this verse should be read: "May the evil eye be far from you, O you of wondrous beauty!" I jest to bring joy.

order.why: Explains the greater influence of serious meaning expressed through humor.
Read the family remembrance and poetic allusion as an affectionate address.
shortened: O servant of the Abha Beauty! You are cherished in this court and accepted and near at the Divine Threshold, and full of culture and distinction, for you are the remembrance of the late Haji and the memorial of Jinab-i-Aqa Siyyid Muhsin the forgiven - both grandfathers were accepted and near in the Most Holy Court. In jest it is written:
This noble one bears the mark of two persons
From Afrasiyab and from Kay Kavus
This servant had the utmost heart attachment in Iraq with those two servants of the Luminary of the horizons.

order.why: Consider the imagined smile of the son present with the writer.
Read playful floral and wine imagery celebrating restored sight.
shortened: Now he will come to you with two eyes like languid narcissus - don't say eyes, say two flasks of pure wine! Don't say hair, say a lock of ambergris! Though he has left no trace of the ambergris with scissors, perhaps fearing whiteness would show, for he has pulled out the roots of his beard. It's not apparent - that is, he has become young. He was weak but has become strong, and like a ball rolls in the field of joy.

order.why: Follow the extended military metaphor for troublesome dentures.
shortened: Now with teeth removed, he has taken in his mouth a new string of pearls lined up like a row of soldiers. Its adornment exceeds the defeated first force, and its order and arrangement is more attractive. However, since this new force consists of foreigners and strangers, they are not as obedient and compliant as the previous native and familiar force. Sometimes they arrange battle lines at the borders and create havoc, plundering the tablecloth and feast. Sometimes they cause corruption in the realm of the mouth itself and produce burning inflammation. When their sedition increases and their rebellion and revolt grows, there is no choice but to expel this foreign force from the territory.

Say nothing and do not reveal it, for the allowances and stipends of others have been greatly delayed, and this Pen has become like the treasury of the Ottomans and Persians - from the abundance of allowances and stipends it has beaten the drum of bankruptcy. I have no recourse except to refer all allowances and stipends to the Abha Kingdom, for that treasury is an inexhaustible treasure.

shortened: And the rapid speech of Jinab-i-Furughi proceeded to enumerate names, and like a swift desert steed galloped forth into the field. I quickly took hold of the reins, otherwise the treasures of names would have been exhausted and the steed of Jinab-i-Furughi would not have ceased its prancing, and this page would have become an entire book of names without any stories or addresses or complaints or reproaches or thanksgiving or praise or counsel or guidance accompanying the names.

order.why: Consider the playful medicinal language of a sweet pen.

shortened: He used to have difficulties with the American and European women because of their numerous questions and persistence. Some of these ladies said, "We went there and knocked at his door. We heard no answer. We persisted in knocking, knowing that he was in. We knocked and we knocked. And finally, he said in English, 'Abul-Fazl not here.'" The ladies said, "We were convulsed with laughter. He himself, from the inside, laughed too. And then we departed."

order.why: Keep the reported acknowledgment of indirect persuasion and its child analogy.

Abdul Baha (laughing): You said right. Bravo, bravo (Aferin, Aferin): A young man when he wishes something from the father states his wish with the utmost politeness, but a little child cries, snatches, kicks, and takes what he wants.

order.why: Read the mock charge of usurping the station of service.
shortened: O servant of the loved ones of God! O usurper of this servant of Baha's right! For service to the friends and servitude to the loved ones is the eternal station and everlasting mission of this servant, yet you have usurped my station and move and walk about with perfect boldness.
Fear God! This is my robe - why have you put it on? This crown is my crown - why have you placed it on your head?

order.why: Consider servitude as the meaning of an affectionate name.
shortened: O 'Abdu'l-Husayn! I could find no title sweeter, more pleasant and more attractive than this with which to address you, for this name signifies servitude to the Blessed Beauty. You are 'Abdu'l-Husayn (Servant of Husayn), and the light of both eyes, and accepted and adorned - what more could you want if you succeed in living up to it? For there is nothing in the world of existence more acceptable, more beloved and more renowned than servitude to the Blessed Beauty, and this name indicates that.

order.why: Keep the insistence on servitude beside its severe closing hyperbole.
shortened: If you wish to make mention of this servant, write: dust of the Sacred Threshold, servant at the court of the One, self-effaced in servitude, wanderer in the wilderness of the love of God, lost in the desert of divine love, intoxicated with the wine of God's love, attracted to the lights of the Absolute Beauty - things of this nature. Anything less than this is absolutely unacceptable. If you were here, I would give you quite a beating!

order.why: Read the exaggerated threat in its demand for language of humility, preserving context.
shortened: Either compose and send a ghazal or ode in pure servitude, utter lowliness, complete effacement, and total humility and contrition before this servant, to make up for past offenses and compensate for the excesses, or - though I have never issued a fatwa until now - this time I shall decree that one should seize your head and another your body, one strike with a club and another with a mace, and bring you here running and dragging in bewilderment. And by God, upon arrival you will bow your head to the ground, your feet will be raised high, and you will receive such a severe beating with a stick that henceforth you will forget all obscurity, exaggeration and excess. So choose for yourself what you prefer!

order.why: Keep the reported scheme of pilgrimage and pardon within the letter’s jest.
Read the imagined reunion and confrontation as the source presents it.
shortened: Sometimes he says that since father is constantly traveling and has no fixed abode, therefore he does not send any written pages, and sometimes he says he has grown somewhat lazy and settled down with his loving mother.

And he says fear God and dread Azrael, for soon breaths will be cut off and we will hasten to that other world and find each other - then we will grab each other by the collar and it will come to fists and slaps and shouting and pistols.

He laughed heartily and said: "You steal my house and put it in your camera and you steal my gardens and put them in your camera! And then you take them to America with you! I shall send my lawyer after you!"

order.why: Keep the childhood recollection of laughter at branding sheep attributed.
shortened: I stood there laughing to my heart's content (Here the Beloved laughed also very heartily) at their strange noises, because I had never seen before such a f[u]nny confusi[ng] scene. When the sheep were released from the hands of the shepherds branding them they r[a]n hither and thither like distracted animals and their droll cries were very amusing and comical to the ears of the little child. I laughed so much on that day that tears flowed from my eyes.

shortened: "If all the spirits of the air", laughed 'Abdu'l-Baha, "were to congregate together they could not create a salad! Nevertheless the spirit of man is powerful; for the spirit of man can soar in the firmament of knowledge, can discover realities, can confer life, can receive the divine Glad-Tidings. Is not this greater than making a salad?"

order.why: Read the guest’s profession of contentment against its cost to the host.

shortened: While he was in the height of 'smoking', suddenly the door was opened and to his surprise the teacher walked in and a column of smoke escaped into the open air.

When he was face to face with his pupil he began to upbraid and censure him for thus wantonly disobeying the Command of his noble father, intimating that if he came to know about this, he would surely punish him severely. To the amazement of the teacher the pupil did not show any sign of agitation but in calm and dignified manner asked him to be seated and he would present his case to his impartial judgement.

'When our holy prophet' the pupil said 'declared his divine mission to the world all the animate creatures and inanimate objects prostrated before him, obeyed his command and offered to them their allegiance, save this accurse[d] and execrable tobacco. It arose in rebellion against its rightful Lord. It is only for this all-sufficient reason that I am subjecting it to smoke as a just punishment for its diabolic disobedience.'
The teacher listening to this religious explanation exclaimed with evident eagerness[:] If it is so, then let me smoke it too;- so that I may also gain the reward of paradise!

order.why: Read the competing scriptural appeals in the reported scholar’s refusal to answer.

Then the Master laughed and said: 'In either case he has not understood.

On the bill of fare was a statement saying: 'Do not eat the first courses. The last one is the best.' This person was a Syrian. I began to eat, but he did not. I repeatedly urged him to eat, but he said: 'No.' At the end of the dinner they brought a course which we could not eat at all. The Syrian tasted it and then left it. He became very disappointed. He said: 'I have eaten nothing. Bring me some food.' The waiter said: 'I cannot, it is against the rule.' It was very hard for him. He remained hungry and it had cost him a pound.

This started a panic and the members of the splendid Caravan began to run about like wild rabbits hither and thither but being in the center of a plain there was no way to escape.

I asked them to take me to the stable to see these miserable fellows. It was a very ludicrous an[d] laughable sight!

order.why: Read the letter’s ironic feast of blows as an account of mistreatment.

As soon as they met the deceived sister, she served them a rich and sweet slap, and the oppressed leaf handmaiden of Baha, your mother, and the young brother received a full course of slaps, beatings, blows and strikes. Bon appétit! You missed quite a colorful spread - sweet delicacies, shelled pistachios and salted almonds.
And afterward, to aid digestion, false accusations were also raised against them - that they had raised hands in aggression and cried out in tyranny and self-pride.

Keep the recalled childhood treatment of a sick man attributed and open to ethical reflection.
