shortened: Five minutes passed, no movement, ten, fifteen minutes, half an hour, no sign of life. The minutes grew heavy and strained. They looked at each other with wonder in their eyes. Then with another laughter and motion of the arms left the room and gathered around the mat. One of them on tip-toe neared and cautiously took away the mat. Wonder of wonder! the man was dead! Then these men carried him on their shoulders with laughter and singing, took him to the undertaker with laughter, washed his body while laughing and buried him under the earth with the roar and thunder of laughter. It was a most phenomenal event!

order.why: Consider the sick wood-chopper’s weariness and the reflection on continuing work.
Read the reported tree-and-ant rebuke to an opposing editor.
shortened: Thy example is like unto the ant who scaled a high, old poplar tree and once reaching on its top, it tried to shake the tree and uproot it. The poplar tree laughed at the ant and said: Dost thou not know that I have experienced many storms, gales, hurricanes and wild tempestuous nights! and now thou little ant hast come to shake and uproot me! Vain is thy thought!

order.why: Consider the remembered reply to repeated complaints in its particular attribution.
Close with the reported country absent from an ordinary map, inviting a different kind of seeing.

questions: What makes the opening wireless exchange encouraging, and how might the same words work differently with another listener?
How do the letters join playful exaggeration with affection, fatigue, service, or consolation?
Which stories reveal a gap between what a person professes and what that person does, and what helps us recognize that gap in ourselves?
How does Ecclesiastes’ pairing of laughter and weeping illuminate the timing and purpose of humor?
What changes when a joke moves from a private relationship into a written report, especially when it involves power, suffering, or a stereotype?
How might humor help a community become more truthful and compassionate while remaining attentive to those who bear the cost of a joke?

references.label: 1 · Ecclesiastes 3:1–8 · A time to laugh
references.note: Read the King James Version’s sequence of paired seasons, including weeping and laughter, silence and speech. Compare this attention to timing with the compilation’s many purposes for jest. Consider how the same form of speech may console in one setting and be ill judged in another, without assuming that the two texts offer identical accounts of joy.

subjects.displayTitle: Degrees of spirit: one bounty, differing capacities
subjects.introduction: Rain falling into a square pool takes a square shape, into a six-sided pool a hexagon; the water itself has no geometry. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá uses this image, and that of one sun lighting stone and glass differently, to explain how a single divine bounty is received according to the capacity of each thing. The mineral coheres, the plant grows, the animal senses, the human being reasons and investigates, and beyond these lies the spirit of faith, a life that natural powers cannot generate. The word spirit shifts its meaning as it moves through these degrees, and learning to hear that shift is part of the discipline. Aristotle, ordering nutrition, perception and thought, asks a different question about soul and body [1]. From here the path leads into the arcs of descent and ascent, the principle that each higher realm encompasses the lower, and the insistence that progress takes place within one’s own degree. Yet the deepest question is not classification but receptivity: what a mind and a character must become to receive more of the life already poured out everywhere.
subjects.arc: Begin with images of one bounty and varied reception, clarify the meanings of spirit, examine capacities and kinds of progress, then return to humility, education, and spiritual life.

order.why: Open with the rain and differently shaped pools as an image of reception.
shortened: God's grace is like the rain that cometh down from heaven: the water is not bounded by the limitations of form, yet on whatever place it poureth down, it taketh on limitations---dimensions, appearance, shape---according to the characteristics of that place. In a square pool, the water, previously unconfined, becometh a square; in a six-sided pool it becometh a hexagon, in an eight-sided pool an octagon, and so forth. The rain itself hath no geometry, no limits, no form, but it taketh on one form or another, according to the restrictions of its vessel. In the same way, the Holy Essence of the Lord God is boundless, immeasurable, but His graces and splendors become finite in the creatures, because of their limitations, wherefore the prayers of given persons will receive favorable answers in certain cases.

order.why: Invite attention to divine signs in trees, blossoms, and stones.
shortened: And whensoever thou dost gaze upon creation all entire, and dost observe the very atoms thereof, thou wilt note that the rays of the Sun of Truth are shed upon all things and shining within them, and telling of that Day-Star's splendours, Its mysteries, and the spreading of Its lights. Look thou upon the trees, upon the blossoms and fruits, even upon the stones. Here too wilt thou behold the Sun's rays shed upon them, clearly visible within them, and manifested by them.

order.why: Read the rays appearing according to each reality’s capacity.
Follow the reported sunlight analogy into distinct meanings of spirit and faith.
shortened: The spirit is a divine bounty that has shone upon all created things, and all created things have received a portion and share of that bounty, like the sun which shines upon all earthly creatures, for all existing things on earth are nurtured by the sun's bounty and receive its rays and light. However, this bounty appears in each rank according to the capacity of that rank. The sun's ray has one effect and radiance in mineral bodies, but in transparent bodies it has another manifestation and appearance. Though there is but one sun, its manifestation varies in different bodies.
Similarly, the spirit's manifestation in the degrees of existence is according to the requirements of those degrees.

But when spiritual people speak of the spirit, they do not mean this spirit. They mean that eternal spirit, that life of faith, that spirit of which Christ says man must be baptized with it, and until he is baptized with that spirit he cannot enter the Kingdom of God.

order.why: Keep the question about mind, spirit, and soul with its categorical answer.
shortened: Question: What is the difference between mind, spirit, and soul?
Answer: It was already explained that, in general, spirit is divided into five categories: the vegetable spirit, the animal spirit, the human spirit, the spirit of faith, and the Holy Spirit.

order.why: Read the full distinction of five kinds of spirit and their functions.
Compare the separate account’s explicit distinction between natural capacities and scriptural Spirit.
shortened: The vegetable spirit is the virtue augmentative, or growing or vegetative faculty, which results from the admixture of the simple elements, with the co-operation of water, air and heat.
The animal spirit is the virtue perceptive resulting from the admixture and absorption of the vital elements generated in the heart, which apprehend sense-impressions.
The human spirit consists of the rational, or logical, reasoning faculty, which apprehends general ideas and things intelligible and perceptible.

Now these "spirits" are not reckoned as Spirit in the terminology of the Scriptures and the usage of the people of the Truth, inasmuch as the laws governing them are as the laws which govern all phenomenal being (i.e., all existences belonging to the phenomenal or material universe, called "the world of generation and corruption"), in respect to generation, corruption, production, change and reversion, as is clearly indicated in the Gospel where it says: "Let the dead bury their dead;" "That which is born of the flesh is flesh, and that which is born of the Spirit is Spirit"; inasmuch as he who would bury these dead was alive with the vegetative, animal and rational human soul, yet did Christ--to whom be glory!--declare such dead and devoid of life, in that this person was devoid of the Spirit of Faith, which is the Kingdom of God.

order.why: Read the different fourfold classification and its acknowledgment of further spirits.
shortened: Know thou that spirits are divided into the animal spirit, the human spirit, the divine spirit, and the heavenly spirit.

The divine spirit, which is of God's command, represents the holy power, divine confirmations, heavenly assistance, divine knowledge, and celestial sciences with which God aids whomsoever He willeth among His righteous servants. Through it they attain mystic revelations and undoubted visions, win the complete preceding mercy and abundant grace, enter the garden of oneness and the divine paradise, and rejoice and delight in what God hath given them of His bounty, thanking Him for His favors and blessings.

As for the heavenly spirit, it is a holy essence, a perfect word, a complete sign, the mystery of existence, and the reality hidden from the eyes of all beings. It is the Supreme Pen, the Most Merciful Soul, and the manifestation of Truth from the dawning-place of creation and its sun at the point of invention. This is specifically for the Prophets in the worlds of creation.

Besides these spirits which I have explained and mentioned to thee, God hath created spirits beyond count or reckoning, including the vegetable spirit, the celestial spirit, the spirit of might, and the intellectual spirit.

order.why: Keep the concise account of innumerable spirits distinct from a closed inventory.
shortened: Know that spirits are divided into animal spirit, human spirit, divine spirit, and heavenly spirit.

Beyond these spirits that I have explained and mentioned to you, God has created countless other spirits, including the vegetable spirit, the angelic spirit, the celestial spirit, and the intellectual spirit.

order.why: Read the reported changing meanings of soul through development and second birth.
shortened: As to the question concerning the soul, know thou, verily, that "soul" is a term applied to numerous realities, according to the exigencies of the following relations with respect to development in the world of existence:
(1) In the mineral kingdom, soul is called "latent force," silently working for the disintegration of the substance of the mineral.

(2) In the vegetable kingdom it is called "virtue augmentative" or the power of growth, which attracts and absorbs the delicate materials of inorganic substance found in the mineral kingdom of matter, and transforms them into the condition of growth.

(3) In the animal kingdom it is called "sense perception" or instinct. This term soul, as applied to the animal kingdom, is also a natural quality resulting from the mixture of the elements, and it appears from their mingling and combination, for it is a quality which results from the composition of bodies (organisms), and is dispersed at their decomposition.
(4) In the human world, soul signifies the "rational being" or mind.

(5) If the angelic aspect becomes more powerful, and the divine power and brightness surround man, then the second birth takes place, and eternal life is found at this point. Man becomes then the noblest among creatures.

order.why: Consider the reported meanings of spirit while retaining its historical ether analogy.
shortened: The word "spirit" has several different significations, or rather there are several degrees of spirit. Spirit in the vegetable world is the life of plants- the power by virtue of which they grow. Spirit in animals confers the capacity of sensation upon physical bodies compounded of associated elements. By virtue of it animals see, hear, feel, and have other sensations.
Spirit in man is the perceiving soul, able to understand the realities of things and predominating over all things else. The spirit of faith endows man with the capacity to love God and to know God.
The spirit of faith is like the ether regarded as the vehicle of light. Etheric matter is found everywhere; but only where it is in undulation does light appear.

order.why: Keep the reported distinction between received bounty and the Spirit of God.
shortened: The Bounty of God is bestowed upon the mineral, the vegetable, animal, and man, but their life, or essence, is not the Spirit of God.

order.why: Read the explicit clarification that spirit here means existence and life.
shortened: You ask about the soul and its multiple stations. People have concluded that it is a single reality which multiplies according to ranks and stations, for it progresses from the lower realm to the higher realm - like the progression of the mineral from the realm of solidity to the realm of growth, and the progression of the plant from the realm of growth to the realm of sensation. When it reaches the human realm it becomes determined and individualized with complete determinations. And when it is baptized by the Holy Spirit, it attains eternal life.

This matter is correct, but what is meant by spirit is existence and life, for existence has a single concept that is not multiple. Existence has ranks, and in each rank it has determination, individuation and special capacity. For example, the mineral, plant, animal and human realms are all in the realm of existence, and none of these realities is deprived of that concept.

order.why: Consider grades of spirit in the Tablet to Dr Forel and the reality beyond comprehension.
Read common material composition alongside differentiated functions.
shortened: When we view the world of creation, we find that all living things may be classified under two aspects of existence. First, they possess bodies composed of material substance common to all -- whether vegetable, animal or human. This is their point of agreement or, as it is philosophically termed, their point of contact. Second, they vary and differ from each other in degree and function -- that is to say, in their respective kingdoms. This is their point of distinction and differentiation.

order.why: Keep the public address’s shared bodily ties and distinguishing features together.
shortened: When we look upon the world of existence, we realize that all material things have a common bond; and yet, on the other hand, there are certain points of distinction between them. For instance, all earthly objects have common bodily ties. The minerals, vegetables and animals have elemental bodies in common with each other. Likewise, they have place in the order of creation.

order.why: Read the three categories and the human combination of their perfections.
shortened: When we examine all things with the eye of discernment, we observe that they are generally confined to three categories: mineral, vegetable, and animal. Thus there are three classes of beings and each class has its associated species. Man is the most distinguished species in that he combines the perfections of all three classes--that is, he possesses a material body, the power of growth, and the power of sensation. Beyond the mineral, vegetable and animal perfections, however, he also possesses a special perfection of which other created things are bereft, namely, the perfections of the mind.

order.why: Compare the public address’s fourfold classification and emphasis on investigation.
Read the public address’s sequence of growth, perception, and reflection.
Keep the reported three general classes and their additional capacities.
Read the reported cumulative account addressed to a rabbi.
Consider the reported examples of intellectual understanding beyond immediate sensation.
Explore the reported power of knowledge to make shared discovery available to a person.
Keep the reported human being as the result of the globe’s kingdoms.
shortened: Regard this globe. Its divisions are mineral, vegetable and animal. Man is the result of all these; therefore man is the result of all existence here.

order.why: Read the reported chain of existence and its description of imperceptible merging.
Keep the public address’s progressive classification in its argumentative context.
Retain the brief distinction of degrees in contingent existence.
shortened: In the realm of existence - that is, existence which is a mental concept and is contingent - there are degrees. The first degree is mineral, then comes the vegetable degree.

order.why: Read the succinct account of each kingdom’s necessary powers.
shortened: Each kingdom of creation is endowed with its necessary complement of attributes and powers. The mineral possesses inherent virtues of its own kingdom in the scale of existence. The vegetable possesses the qualities of the mineral plus an augmentative virtue, or power of growth. The animal is endowed with the virtues of both the mineral and vegetable plane plus the power of intellect.

order.why: Make explicit the distinction between innate degree and moral good or evil.
Read the question about election with its answer on diversity and each degree’s perfection.
shortened: Question: Christ says in the Gospel: "many are called, but few are chosen", and in the Qur'an it is written: "He singleth out for His mercy whomsoever He pleaseth." What is the wisdom of this?

Answer: Know that the order and perfection of the universe require that existence should appear in countless forms. Created things cannot therefore be realized in a single degree, station, manner, kind, or species: Differences of degree, distinctions in form, and a multiplicity of kinds and species are inevitable.

Now, so long as the degrees of created things are different, some will naturally rank above the others. Thus, since the election of certain creatures, such as man, for the highest degree; the maintenance of others, such as plants, in the middle degree; and the relegation of yet others, such as minerals, to the lowest degree are each and all due to the divine will and purpose, it follows that the singling out of man for the highest degree is through the grace of God, and that the differences among men with regard to spiritual attainments and heavenly perfections are likewise due to the choice of the All-Merciful.

As for material beings, they are not to be blamed, judged, or held accountable for their own degrees and stations. Thus the mineral, the plant, and the animal are each acceptable in their own degree, but if they were to remain deficient in that degree they would be blameworthy, the degree itself being wholly perfect.

order.why: Consider the reported need for more than humanity alone to make a world.
Place differentiated perfections within the reported encounter of East and West.
Follow the public address’s interpretation of cohesion and affinity as degrees of love.
shortened: We declare that love is the cause of the existence of all phenomena and that the absence of love is the cause of disintegration or nonexistence. Love is the conscious bestowal of God, the bond of affiliation in all phenomena.

The power of cohesion expressed in the mineral kingdom is in reality love or affinity manifested in a low degree according to the exigencies of the mineral world. We take a step higher into the vegetable kingdom where we find an increased power of attraction has become manifest among the composing elements which form phenomena. Through this degree of attraction a cellular admixture is produced among these elements which make up the body of a plant. Therefore, in the degree of the vegetable kingdom there is love. We enter the animal kingdom and find the attractive power binding together single elements as in the mineral, plus the cellular admixture as in the vegetable, plus the phenomena of feelings or susceptibilities. We observe that the animals are susceptible to certain affiliation and fellowship and that they exercise natural selection. This elemental attraction, this admixture and selective affinity is love manifest in the degree of the animal kingdom.

order.why: Read the stone’s attraction as the address’s lowest-degree expression of love.
Consider universal attraction, diverse forms, and human yearning in the Tablet’s account.
shortened: O thou who art yearning to discover! The discoverers of the mysteries of existence and those who comprehend the qualities and hidden secrets hold that a wondrous force of attraction and a strange magnetic power of connection permeates and encompasses all these infinite beings and successive contingent things, both physical and spiritual, and is equally present in them all. And it is through this universal force that the individual essences of the different simple elements come together, and due to the diversity and differences of parts, the multiplication and contrast of the infinite diverse realities of existing things come into being.
And in human reality it has become the power of yearning, bringing about enthusiasm and passion and attraction.

order.why: Keep the reported cohesion of a stone and purification into a mirror.
Read the reported logos and magnetism in its theological vocabulary.
shortened: This is the way and manner how the creative and eternally creating (engendering) word of God, that is, the logos, is manifested and produces its effect in all atoms. In the mineral kingdom, the logos shows itself as attraction and repulsion, thus as earth magnetism.

order.why: Attribute the reported claims about mineral life and scientific proof to their historical source.
shortened: When we look with the eye of truth upon all created things, we observe that every created thing possesseth life. In ancient philosophy it was held that mineral matter was lifeless, but through profound investigation it hath now been established that minerals too possess life, and scientific proofs in modern philosophy have been advanced to demonstrate this. We shall speak briefly and say that all created things possess life, but the life of each creation is according to its capacity. For example, in the mineral kingdom there is life, but it is exceedingly weak, like the embryo in the mother's womb which, though possessing a spirit, is very feeble.

order.why: Keep the brief reported appeal to scientific discoveries attributed rather than editorially confirmed.
shortened: Yes, the latest scientific discoveries prove to us that even mineral has some form of life, and that it also needs water for its existence.

order.why: Read the reported account of attraction, growth, and capacity.
shortened: I thought of how the spirit radiates in all the realms of nature according to the receptive degree. In the mineral world the spirit shows itself, but limited to that mineral condition. It is proved through science that the mineral has the power of attraction, the vegetable has the power of growth; life is according to capacity.

order.why: Consider the reported relativity of sensibility to a kingdom’s degree.
shortened: Abdul Baha said: These lower kingdoms are not without certain sensibilities, but compared to man they are without sense. There is nothing without life: The spirit is according to its degree in creation.

order.why: Read the reported plant sensitivity as a distinction of degree.
Keep the reported observation of varying sensitivities in its own wording.
shortened: Then he spoke about the sensitiveness of the plants and how they have a degree of "feeling" according to their environments. There are various degrees of sensitiveness in all the Kingdoms of creation.

order.why: Read the reported explanation of plant and animal spirit as an answer in context.
Consider the public address’s language of progression across kingdoms.
Keep the reported compressed sequence of life’s progress.
Read the reported molecule’s journey as an account of successive forms and experiences.
Distinguish the reported return of bodily elements from annihilation.
Keep the reported Cosmic Spirit account and its strong metaphysical claims in their attribution.
Read the reported ascent toward further divine worlds.
Set the reported progression within a kingdom beside the accounts of passage through kingdoms.
shortened: All beings are divided into the mineral, vegetable, animal and human kingdoms. The mineral has the chance to advance in its own kingdom--as coal has the chance to advance into diamonds, it can advance into the highest station in its own kingdom, but it cannot attain a step in the vegetable kingdom, for it has not the power of growth. As to the vegetable kingdom, a plant has the opportunity to reach the highest stage in its own kingdom, but it is not possible to leave its kingdom and enter into that of the animal. And the animal cannot enter the human kingdom.

order.why: Read the concise reported restriction of progress to its own degree.
shortened: When one considers the mineral, vegetable, animal and human kingdoms, it is observed that each progresses within its own degree.

order.why: Keep the explicit statement about spirits not returning to this world.
shortened: The vegetable spirit, the animal spirit, and the human spirit---the rational soul, that is---do not return after death to this world of the "first creation".

order.why: Uses the kingdoms of existence to explain differing capacities and higher life.
Read the reported human position at the end of the descending arc.
Keep the companion reported statement about the mineral’s position.
Consider divine names, gradated realities, and the ascending and descending arcs.
shortened: Praise be to God Who hath ever caused His Names and Attributes to penetrate the degrees of existence; Who hath made the effects of those Names and Attributes to shine resplendent and their signs to be firmly established in both the hidden and manifest worlds. By them He hath made the Sanctified Realities, they who are the Recipients of the grace of God and the Bearers of glad-tidings, to be the sole Revealers of His Being, and hath caused them to move in the firmament of perfection in descending and ascending arcs. He hath ordained them to be the origin and cause of existence in the world of creation and the source of gradated realities in the degrees of being.

order.why: Read the Bab’s distinct ordering of eight worlds without collapsing it into other classifications.
Consider the seven days interpreted as ranks, retaining the terminal omission.
shortened: But the second meaning is that the days represent ranks: the first rank is the mineral kingdom, the second rank is the vegetable kingdom, the third rank is the animal kingdom, the fourth rank is the human rational soul, the fifth rank is the realm of intellect, the sixth rank is the spiritual realm which is the Kingdom, and the seventh rank is that of Oneness, Lordship and Divinity. These ranks culminate in seven. The six ranks are the world of creation and existence, while the seventh rank is the world of Truth and sanctification from the conditions of creation.  Thus this blessed Cycle falls in the seventh rank - it is the mighty Cycle, the new resurrection, the Greater Day of Judgment, the Abha Paradise, and the planting ground of the Tree of Life. Therefore, in reality it has no end or termination....

order.why: Read the Bab’s seven-stage ascent and the inmost heart with the supplied omissions.
Hear the warning that an extended explanation exceeds the listeners’ capacity.
Consider the relation between rank and the limits of comprehension.
shortened: Behold then with true sight and spiritual vision how the realities of created things exist in different ranks and diverse stations. That which exists in a lower rank cannot comprehend, much less inquire about, that which exists in a rank above it. Consider the ranks of mineral, plant, animal and man.

order.why: Keep the reported illustration of the mineral’s inability to comprehend a plant.
shortened: "The mineral kingdom is distinct in its conditions from the vegetable. It is impossible for the mineral to comprehend the powers of the vegetable, which grows and changes from a seed into a flower or tree, drawing its nutriment from earth and air and water. So, again, it is impossible for the vegetable to conceive of the kingdom above it, the animal who powers and senses so entirely transcend its own.

order.why: Read the reported many worlds beyond those presently seen.
Hold the oneness of the world beside its distinct stations and heavenly forms.
shortened: The answer to the first question: the souls of the children of the Kingdom, after their separation from the body, ascend unto the realm of everlasting life. But if ye ask as to the place, know ye that the world of existence is a single world, although its stations are various and distinct.

Those souls who are pure and unsullied, upon the dissolution of their elemental frames, hasten away to the world of God, and that world is within this world. The people of this world, however, are unaware of that world, and are even as the mineral and the vegetable that know nothing of the world of the animal and the world of man.

order.why: Read mineral life as human death as an explicitly relative comparison.
Consider the relative uses of lifelessness and death across kingdoms.
shortened: For example, the mineral kingdom in comparison with the vegetable kingdom is lifeless; also the existence of the animal kingdom in comparison with that of the human is death.

order.why: Keep the reported relative comparison without treating a lower degree as literal nonexistence.
shortened: The mineral has existence, the vegetable has existence, but the existence of the inferior kingdom as compared with the existence of the human kingdom is as non-existence. Even the mineral is living in relation to its own kingdom: but the mineral kingdom in comparison with the vegetable kingdom is non-existent, and the vegetable with the animal is non-existence.

order.why: Read the explicit affirmation that both ignorant and wise souls exist.
shortened: In brief, all souls exist, but the existence of the heedless and the ignorant in comparison to the existence of the perfect and the wise is like nonexistence.

The intention of this discourse is that both the ignorant and the wise possess existence, but the existence of the ignorant is like that of a stone, while the existence of the perfect individual resembleth the existence of man.

order.why: Consider the movement from relative natural life to the life of the Kingdom.
Read the source’s distinction of spiritual heights and depths.
shortened: O thou who art enkindled with the fire of the love of God!

In the world of existence there are higher and lower stations, and the ranks of the highest heaven and the depths of hell are visible, and the zenith of virtues and the nadir of vices are proven and known.

order.why: Hold differences of capacity beside the unity of effulgence.
Read the public address’s need for education, with its internal omission.
shortened: When we look upon the kingdoms of creation below man, we find three forms or planes of existence which await education and development.
As to the human world: It is more in need of guidance and education than the lower creatures.

order.why: Consider the reported gardener and animal examples as images of cultivation.
Read the reported analogy between a flower’s light and human spiritual illumination.
shortened: The flower needs light that it may achieve its fruitage; man needs the light of the Holy Spirit, and the measure of illumination throughout creation is proportionate to the different kingdoms.

order.why: Connect varied human understanding with the need for love and oneness.
shortened: It is clear that human realities differ one from another, that opinions and perceptions vary, and that this divergence of thoughts, opinions, understandings and sentiments among individuals is an essential requirement. For differences of degree in creation are among the essential requirements of existence, which is resolved into countless forms. We stand therefore in need of a universal power which can prevail over the thoughts, opinions and sentiments of all, which can annul these divisions and bring all souls under the sway of the principle of the oneness of humanity. And it is clear and evident that the greatest power in the human world is the love of God.

order.why: Close the linked addresses with hope for growing receptivity and unveiled human virtues.
shortened: This illimitable divine bounty has no beginning and will have no ending. It is moving, circulating and becomes effective wherever capacity is developed to receive it. In every station there is a specialized capacity. Therefore, we must be hopeful that through the bounty and favor of God this spirit of life infusing all created beings shall quicken humanity, and from its bestowals the human world shall become a divine world, this earthly kingdom become the mirror of the realm of Divinity, the virtues and perfections of the world of humanity become unveiled and the image and likeness of God be reflected from this temple.

order.why: Keep the brief statement of one reality and varied names with its internal omission.
Read the supplied parallel translation’s careful distinction between existence and specific spirits.
shortened: In brief, existence hath one signification, but its manifestations, appearances, and attributes vary in every grade and station.     As for the kinds of spirit, these are fixed realities each having its own specification and individualization, particular perfections and attributes, which distinguish one from another. They differ with respect to their essential qualities and what they signify. The mineral spirit, therefore, cannot be compared to the plant spirit, because the latter is the power of growth. The animal spirit, also, is a specialized reality distinct from all besides itself through its attributes and significations, for it is the power of sense perception and volitional movement.

order.why: Retain the supplied provisional account of perishable animal spirit.
Keep the supplied provisional fourfold terminology and further spirits with its omission.
Read the supplied provisional enumeration of spiritual states without completing missing material.
Consider the supplied provisional account of the spirit as a mirror for attributes.
Keep the supplied provisional Divine Spirit passage and its omissions.
Read the supplied provisional ascent through purification and changing limitations.
Keep the supplied pilgrim-note account of five spirits as a distinct witness.
Attribute the supplied appeal to science to its preserved source.
Read the supplied diary passage on matter and energy with its approximate-reference status unchanged.
Retain the supplied parallel statement about relative mineral life.
Consider the supplied Plotinus image of light in its own attribution.
Keep the supplied Plotinus circles of light and the additional material in its citation together.
Read the supplied Pseudo-Dionysius comparison as a distinct philosophical voice.
End with the supplied distinction between limited degrees and unlimited divine outpouring.

questions: How do the rain and sunlight images help explain both unity and difference among created things?
What changes in the meaning of spirit across the passages on growth, sensation, reason, faith, and the Holy Spirit?
How does Aristotle’s treatment of living capacities clarify the comparison, and where does the compilation ask a different kind of question?
How can we distinguish the movement of bodily elements, development within a degree, and spiritual transformation when reading these texts together?
What does the distinction between a difference of capacity and moral good or evil imply for how we regard other people?
How might education, love, and reflection increase receptivity while deepening humility about realities beyond our present understanding?

references.label: 1 · Aristotle, On the Soul II.2–3 · Capacities of living things
references.note: Read Parts 2 and 3 of Book II in J. A. Smith’s translation. Aristotle distinguishes nutrition, sensation, movement, and thought, and asks how their powers belong to soul and body. Compare his ordered capacities with the compilation’s varied uses of spirit, attending especially to what changes when the discussion turns to faith and divine assistance.
